- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the recent 24-day history, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model tends to underestimate; apply upward bias correction by 1–4% for the next 3–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–10 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30-day forecasts — if forecast is >10% above recent 24-day average, adjust downward by 2–5%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (0.0–0.1) and forecast is flat or rising, model underestimates volatility; increase forecast volatility by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- For horizon 30d, model often fails to capture late-period sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after day 15–20, adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for days 20–30.
